themes.title: Promo Codes / Coupons
themes.text: Promo code support at checkout and gift card redemption requested; Orgill FanBuilder coupon integration a Phase 2 priority

themes.title: Apple Pay / Google Pay
themes.text: Digital wallet support described as table stakes; needed for in-store card-present and online checkout

themes.title: ERP/Payment Reconciliation
themes.text: Cash drawer segregation across 15+ branches; merchant ID confusion; duplicate payments and WebTrack API sync failures

themes.title: WebTrack Displacement
themes.text: Actively replaced across 6 accounts; 10% WebTrack adoption jumping to 40% on Toolbx; payment failures and poor mobile UX driving switch

themes.title: ERP Vendor Lock-in
themes.text: ERPs have a stranglehold over tech investment; Epicor API costs rising to $600/mo+, Azure migration failures, support quality declining

themes.title: In-Order Messaging
themes.text: Want to attach messages directly to a specific order for two-way communication with the dealer; not currently offered, noted internally as a candidate for future development

themes.title: Live Pricing / Real-Time Inventory in Portal
themes.text: Confirmed missing from this account's initial portal rollout scope; unclear whether this is a platform limitation or a phased-implementation decision

themes.title: ERP Integration Complexity
themes.text: Sync reliability and API compatibility issues across Sage 100, Spruce, and DMSi Agility causing pricing errors, compliance exposure, and delayed rollouts

themes.title: CC Processing Fees / Surcharging
themes.text: High per-transaction fees eating into margins; state surcharge caps (e.g. Colorado 2%) don't cover actual processing costs

themes.title: Competing E-commerce/POS Platforms
themes.text: Prospects actively evaluating alternatives (GenetiQ, Lightspeed, Paladin, MSI Agility) on pricing and API openness before committing

themes.title: Big-Box & Buying-Group Pressure
themes.text: Buying-group members losing share to Home Depot, Lowe's, and Menards; Builders FirstSource's "builder.com" cited as a Costco-like contractor pricing threat

themes.title: Automated Credit / Reference Checks
themes.text: Toolbx confirmed it currently lacks automated credit-agency pings and reference checks (roadmapped for 2027, not available today); this deal is contingent on matching or exceeding their current credit-app tool on this specific capability

themes.title: Industry-Specific CRM / Quote Management
themes.text: No CRM built for this industry exists -- only generic tools that don't fit. Result: zero quote visibility and a 25,000-quote backlog from manually double-entering everything into their ERP

themes.title: Multi-System Quote-to-Order Tracking
themes.text: Extreme difficulty tracking quotes through to sales orders across multiple systems as data changes, compounded by the manual burden of typing up material lists across counter, sales support, and outside sales

themes.title: Manual Credit-App / Account Setup
themes.text: Integrating approved credit applications into their ERP (BizTrack) is a fully manual process, as is setting up new cash-customer accounts -- both a real administrative burden

themes.title: Legacy POS Displacement
themes.text: Migrating off Paladin due to its outdated web UI and expensive per-computer licensing across six workstations

themes.title: Builder/GC Portal Integration
themes.text: No way to pull purchase orders directly from major builder portals (e.g. DR Horton, SupplyPro) to auto-create orders -- confirmed as a flat gap today, not a config option: "None of those as of right now, no."

themes.title: BOGO / Bundle Promotions
themes.text: Can't run manufacturer bundle promos (e.g. buy-a-tool-get-a-free-battery) on the catalog today -- confirmed directly: "That is not something we support right now"

themes.title: Reverse Tally for Random-Length Lumber
themes.text: Tally tool only works one direction (lengths to total); can't take a target linear footage and calculate the board-length mix needed, unlike a tool this customer used previously

themes.title: In-App Click-to-Call Logging
themes.text: Toolbx's CRM module can't place a call from inside the app with the call automatically logged to the record -- a specific capability the customer named after comparing to HubSpot, which already has it

themes.title: Manual Margin-Based Commission Dashboarding
themes.text: Regional sales managers hand-build margin-filterable commission dashboards in Power BI today; asked if this could be built directly into Toolbx

themes.title: CRM Migration Data-Continuity Risk
themes.text: Customer is timing a CRM switch around when their Salesforce contract lapses, worried about losing data mid-migration -- Toolbx's own rep confirmed the new CRM is still being built out with early customers, not fully mature yet

themes.title: Permit & Job Status Disconnected from ERP
themes.text: No way to link permit/lead data to job status today -- a self-built app tracks permits separately, and confirming whether a "sold" job has actually shipped requires manually checking each one individually

themes.title: AR Notes / Call-Logging Sync to ERP
themes.text: Notes and call logs entered in Toolbx don't pass back into BizTrack -- confirmed directly: "I don't believe those get passed back into biztrack. Those are sort of just managed within toolbx."

themes.title: Buying-Group Dealer Pricing
themes.text: Orgill VP says $2K/month per-site is "a no go" for the majority of CNRG dealers and requests a 40-50% reduction. CDIO independently reached the same conclusion. Vanathy benchmarks against Impact Commerce and Unilog as lower-cost incumbents; separately, EvoX/Spruce at Stones is roughly half of Toolbx pricing.

themes.title: Epicor API Requirement Confusion
themes.text: Franklin purchased the BizTrack API on expiring promotional pricing after being told it was required, then repeatedly heard it may not be needed -- "the mixed signals continue on." Toolbx acknowledges this is a recent Epicor policy shift they are still working through messaging on, affecting all BizTrack third-party integrations. The confusion stalled parallel API/VPN workstreams and slowed implementation.

themes.title: Canadian EFT Payment Support
themes.text: Toolbx does not support EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer) for Canadian payments. Caliper Forest, a Canadian business, relies on EFT as the standard electronic payment method. Customer accepted a manual workaround -- displaying bank info on the payment screen with instructions to send EFT directly -- but noted "the ACH would be probably minimum because it's all EFT in Canada."

themes.title: Eagle SKU Lifecycle Sync
themes.text: Eagle flat-file integration forces manual dual-maintenance of SKU catalogs. Pricing and quantities sync automatically, but adding/removing products and changing discontinued flags requires manual updates in Toolbx. Customer reports other dealers spending "hours a week" on this same workflow and attributes the limitation to Eagle's flat-file architecture.

themes.title: LumberTrack ERP Integration
themes.text: Do it Best asked whether Toolbx CRM could connect to LumberTrack. Scott confirmed it cannot -- the data model is "quite a bit different" from BizTrack. Do it Best volunteered to be an anchor/design partner. Separately, they noted Zendesk is sunsetting CRM support within a year, creating timing alignment for Toolbx CRM adoption.

themes.title: Spruce/ECI Platform Failure Driving Displacement
themes.text: Stones is actively considering leaving Spruce (ECI/Evolution X) -- "it's not going well" on both integration and support. Already has ~150 customers paying online through Spruce but is nearing the decision to "pull the plug." Primary hesitation: migrating existing online-paying customers without disruption. Toolbx offered to waive onboarding fees.

themes.title: ECI Closed-Ecosystem API Barriers
themes.text: ECI/Spruce refuses third-party integrations to push their own Evo X e-commerce, jacking up API prices to deter vendors like Toolbx. Orgill VP says ECI overcharges on payment processing -- "they're ripping them off." 30% of Orgill's customer base is on Spruce. Jim plans to confront Spruce president at their vendor conference dinner.
